# Library multiplayer fixture protocol

Start this fresh F200 world, then connect exactly two real clients whose actual `LuaPlayer.locale` values report `en` and `de`. Initial unchanged locales do not require a locale-change event. Wait for the `rejoin-ready` marker, disconnect and reconnect both clients, then wait for `restart-ready` and the requested `mir5-library-multiplayer-restart` save. Restart the host from that save, reconnect both clients again, and wait for `completed` plus `mir5-native-complete`.

The four latency observations are emitted directly to each executing process's native log as `[MIR5_LIBRARY_PROFILE] first_open`, `search`, `refresh` and `reopen`, followed by the engine-rendered profiler. Saved state and JSON witnesses contain only deterministic completion flags for those labels. Read the actual native log records to qualify timings; flags, profiler object identities and host mocks are not measured latency. No profiler value selects a gameplay or fixture-state transition.

The control requests ten GUI screenshots under `script-output/mir5-library-multiplayer/`: Availability, initial personal view, settled initial view, rejoin and host restart for each client. The initial Availability view contains exactly two terminal Space Age requirement explanations and stays open for 60 ticks before ordinary personal views replace it. After the original initial captures, the same roots, queries and native state are held for 60 ticks before the settled pair is requested, without reopening the Library. A further 60 ticks lets that pair render before `rejoin-ready` permits client disconnection. This separates a persistent layout defect from a transient initial capture; it does not declare either image correct. Screenshots become rendering evidence only after external PNG readback confirms the files; a headless request is not a rendering result.

After the initial personal views are open, the fixture keeps their public browser root and query objects, marks only the four named science-pack prerequisites researched, and queues two real levels of `recipe-prod-research_gears-1`. Its fixture-local `settings-updates.lua` reduces only that stream’s count and time so two actual lab completions can be observed within the bounded disposable world; it does not qualify ordinary cost or time tuning. The empty lab receives one of each named pack initially, then receives one more of each only after the first actual completion and its level-two/one-queued/UI witnesses. This staged fixture feeding keeps the total at two per named pack. The earlier all-at-once run stopped short of its second completion; the separate staged run40133428618 completed both, without establishing the earlier failure's cause. The control requires public force queue lengths 2→1→0 plus native started/finished events, `by_script == false`, level three, the resulting +20% iron-gear-wheel productivity, and zero remaining packs before it preserves the post-lab snapshot.

The fixture then queues and cancels one third level through `LuaForce.cancel_current_research`, requiring the native cancellation callback and no third laboratory completion. It creates a separate foreign force and requires that its initial gear level/productivity and both already-open player views remain independent. It never imports MIR internals, reads MIR storage, or synthesizes native events. The rejoin and host-restart stages still verify the stored post-lab witness and all ten client-local captures. The completed native session from run40133428618 retains its original eight-capture protocol and separate initial German clipping finding; these added captures require a new exact-input execution.
